intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's culinary soul.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's iconic electric town, visiting multi-floor electronics shops, retro gaming arcades, maid cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Experience the intersection of Japanese pop culture and technology innovation firsthand.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, strolling through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Witness morning prayers, explore the five-story pagoda, and soak in centuries of Edo-period culture.

experiences.name: Shibuya and Harajuku Street Food and Fashion Culture Tour
experiences.description: Navigate the world-famous Shibuya Crossing, then head to Takeshita Street in Harajuku for crepes, cotton candy, and quirky street fashion. Explore Omotesando's upscale dining alleys for a contrast of Tokyo's modern culinary and cultural identity.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated digital art installations where technology and culture merge into breathtaking immersive environments. Walk through infinite light forests, crystal worlds, and interactive digital ecosystems that redefine the boundary between art and viewer.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check in to your boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short walk to the Tsukiji Outer Market (just steps from your hotel). Browse fresh seafood stalls, tamagoyaki egg shops, and local vendors. Pick up affordable street snacks like grilled scallops or fish-on-a-stick to fuel your first afternoon in Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront toward Hamarikyu Gardens (entry ¥300). Watch the sunset over Tokyo Bay from the gardens, then head back to the Tsukiji area for a relaxed first dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab onigiri (rice balls) from a 7-Eleven or FamilyMart convenience store for around ¥150–200 each.
meals.lunch: Street food snacks at Tsukiji Outer Market — try maguro (tuna) skewers or tamagoyaki for ¥200–500 per item.
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area ramen shop — a hearty bowl of ramen costs ¥700–900. Try Ramen Nagi or a local tonkotsu spot nearby.

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless subway and bus travel throughout the trip. Load ¥3,000–5,000 initially. Keep jet lag in mind — don't overdo it on Day 1.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Tsukiji Outer Market early (opens around 5:00–6:00 AM) for a proper morning exploration. Sample fresh sushi breakfasts, tamagoyaki, and pickled vegetables directly from vendors. This is one of Tokyo's most authentic local food experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and anime district. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Bic Camera, retro game shops, and maid cafes. Window shop or pick up budget tech gadgets and second-hand electronics.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for the evening lights — the neon signs are spectacular after dark. Explore the arcades (game centers) for ¥100 per play. Head back to Tsukiji area via subway.

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — a 5-piece set costs around ¥500–800 at stalls like Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi.
meals.lunch: Akihabara ramen or curry — try a Japanese curry rice set (katsu curry) for ¥700–1,000 at a local chain like CoCo Ichibanya.
meals.dinner: Akihabara gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya — filling and costs only ¥400–600.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best experienced in the afternoon and evening when it's fully buzzing. Many electronics shops offer tax-free shopping for tourists with passport — bring yours.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Asakusa — Tokyo's most traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry), Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional souvenirs like ningyo-yaki cakes and kokeshi dolls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River to Ueno Park (free entry). Explore the park's cherry blossom paths (late April may still have some blooms), and visit the Tokyo National Museum for a deep dive into Japanese history and culture (entry ¥1,000).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air street market selling everything from fresh seafood to cheap clothing and snacks. Great for people-watching and budget shopping.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea from 7-Eleven for under ¥400.
meals.lunch: Asakusa area — try a traditional tempura tendon (tempura rice bowl) at a local restaurant for ¥900–1,200.
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market street food — grilled yakitori skewers, takoyaki (octopus balls), and cold Asahi beer for around ¥800–1,200 total.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. The Nakamise Shopping Street opens around 10:00 AM. Ueno Park is a 10-minute walk from Asakusa or a short subway ride.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Shibuya — take the subway from Tsukiji. Start at the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing, one of the busiest intersections in the world. Visit the Hachiko Statue, then explore Shibuya 109 fashion building and the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill to Harajuku and Takeshita Street — Tokyo's quirky youth fashion hub. Browse colorful shops, try crepes (¥400–600), and soak in the vibrant street culture. Then visit the peaceful Meiji Shrine (free entry) nearby for a cultural contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shibuya for the evening. Observe the Scramble Crossing lit up at night from the free observation deck at Scramble Square (free floor) or Mag's Park rooftop. Explore Shibuya's izakayas (Japanese pubs) for drinks and small plates.

meals.breakfast: Grab a morning set at Doutor Coffee near Shibuya station — coffee and toast for ¥400–500.
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepes and street snacks — budget ¥600–800 for a filling crepe and drink.
meals.dinner: Shibuya izakaya — order edamame, karaage (fried chicken), and a beer. Budget ¥1,200–1,800 per person at a chain like Torikizoku (all items ¥330).

day_by_day.notes: Saturdays in Harajuku are especially vibrant. Meiji Shrine is a 5-minute walk from Harajuku station. Wear comfortable shoes — this day involves significant walking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (entry ¥500) in the morning — a stunning park with late-blooming cherry trees and French, English, and Japanese garden sections. Perfect for a peaceful Sunday morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's Kabukicho entertainment district and the Golden Gai — a maze of tiny atmospheric bars packed into narrow alleys. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck for panoramic city views (open until 22:30, free).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku at night — the neon lights of Kabukicho are iconic. Explore the Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) alley for tiny yakitori stalls and smoky atmosphere. Very budget-friendly for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or bakery near hotel — pick up a melon pan (sweet bread) and coffee for ¥300.
meals.lunch: Shinjuku depachika (department store basement food hall) — grab bento boxes or sushi sets for ¥600–900.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori — tiny skewers of grilled chicken and vegetables for ¥150–200 each. Budget ¥1,000–1,500 for a satisfying dinner with a beer.

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely free — one of the best views in the city. Golden Gai bars are tiny (5–8 seats) and atmospheric but may have cover charges of ¥500–1,000.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Odaiba — a futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Reach it via the scenic Yurikamome monorail (¥330 one way) from Shimbashi station. Visit teamLab Borderless digital art museum (book in advance, ¥3,200) for a mind-blowing immersive tech-art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's free attractions — the life-size Gundam statue at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, the retro Decks Tokyo Beach mall, and the iconic Rainbow Bridge views. Visit the free Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science) lobby exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Tokyo Bay from Odaiba Beach — free and spectacular with Rainbow Bridge in the background. Take the monorail back to Tsukiji area.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel before departing — onigiri set for ¥350.
meals.lunch: DiverCity Tokyo Plaza food court — ramen or udon sets for ¥700–1,000.
meals.dinner: Back in Tsukiji — try a local soba noodle restaurant near the hotel for ¥700–900.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless is a must for tech and culture lovers — book tickets online in advance as they sell out. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself offers great views of the bay. Miraikan full entry is ¥630 if you want to explore inside.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old downtown (shitamachi) neighborhoods. Walk through Yanaka Cemetery (free), a peaceful and historic space with old cherry trees. Explore the charming Yanaka Ginza shopping street with traditional craft shops and local snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nezu Shrine (free entry) — a smaller, less-crowded alternative to Fushimi Inari with beautiful torii gate tunnels. Then visit nearby Nezu Museum (¥1,300) for exquisite Japanese art collections in a serene garden setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Akihabara for a second evening visit — this time focus on the retro gaming culture. Visit Super Potato retro game shop and explore the multi-floor arcades. Try a maid cafe experience (budget ¥500–1,000 for a drink and a performance).

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street food — freshly grilled menchi katsu (minced meat cutlet) for ¥200–300.
meals.lunch: Local teishoku (set meal) restaurant in Yanaka — rice, miso soup, grilled fish, and sides for ¥800–1,000.
meals.dinner: Akihabara — try a tech-themed or anime-themed restaurant, or grab affordable donburi (rice bowl) for ¥600–800.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is a wonderful contrast to Tokyo's modern image — very authentic and photogenic. The neighborhood is best explored on foot. Nezu Shrine is far less crowded than Senso-ji and very peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ginza — Tokyo's upscale shopping and arts district, just a short walk or subway ride from Tsukiji. Window shop the luxury boutiques (free!), visit the free Itoya stationery flagship store (a stationery lover's paradise), and explore the Sony Park exhibit space.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tsukiji Hongan-ji Temple (free entry) near your hotel — a stunning Indo-Saracenic style Buddhist temple. Then head to the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300) for a second, more relaxed visit and tea ceremony at the traditional teahouse (¥510 including matcha and wagashi).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sumida River promenade at dusk — beautiful views of the city lights reflecting on the water. Explore the local Tsukiji neighborhood for dinner at a restaurant you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Ginza bakery — Kimuraya Bakery (established 1869) near Ginza station sells iconic anpan (sweet red bean buns) for ¥200–300.
meals.lunch: Ginza area lunch special — many restaurants offer affordable weekday lunch sets for ¥800–1,200 (much cheaper than dinner prices).
meals.dinner: Tsukiji neighborhood izakaya — try a local spot serving grilled seafood and cold Sapporo beer for ¥1,200–1,800.

day_by_day.notes: Ginza is expensive to shop but free to explore. The lunch set culture in Japan means you can eat at nice restaurants affordably at midday. Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse matcha experience is excellent value.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Ikebukuro — a less touristy alternative to Shibuya and Shinjuku with great local culture. Visit the Sunshine City complex and explore the free floors. Check out the Pokemon Center Mega Tokyo (free to browse) and the large Animate anime goods store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ikebukuro's Otome Road — the female-oriented manga and anime shopping street. Visit Tokyu Hands multi-floor lifestyle store for unique Japanese design goods. Head to the free observation deck at Sunshine 60 Sky Circus (¥800 for the full experience).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ikebukuro's local dining scene — the area has excellent Chinese-Japanese fusion food and ramen. Visit the underground restaurant floors of Sunshine City for affordable dinner options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store — pick up a breakfast sandwich and coffee for ¥400.
meals.lunch: Ikebukuro ramen — try the famous Ikebukuro-style ramen at a local shop for ¥800–1,000.
meals.dinner: Ikebukuro Chinese-Japanese restaurant — gyoza dumplings, mapo tofu, and rice for ¥900–1,300.

day_by_day.notes: Ikebukuro is very popular with young locals and has a great authentic atmosphere. The Pokemon Center is free to browse — great for tech/pop culture fans. Tokyu Hands is a wonderful store for unique Japanese gifts and gadgets.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Kawagoe (Little Edo) — about 1 hour from Ikebukuro by train (¥470 one way). Explore the beautifully preserved Edo-period kurazukuri (clay-walled warehouse) merchant district. Visit the iconic Bell Tower and browse traditional sweet shops on Candy Alley (Kashiya Yokocho).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tokyo and visit Koenji — a bohemian neighborhood known for vintage clothing shops, record stores, and indie cafes. Explore the covered shopping arcades and browse second-hand vinyl records and retro tech items.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Koenji's local live music scene — many small live houses (venues) have affordable entry fees of ¥1,000–1,500. Return to Tsukiji via subway.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before the Kawagoe trip.
meals.lunch: Kawagoe — try imoni (sweet potato) dishes and traditional unagi (eel) rice for ¥900–1,200 at a local restaurant.
meals.dinner: Koenji neighborhood — casual Japanese curry or ramen at a local shop for ¥700–900.

day_by_day.notes: Kawagoe is a fantastic day trip for culture lovers — feels like stepping back in time. The Seibu Shinjuku line or Tobu Tojo line from Ikebukuro makes it easy to reach. Koenji has a very different, artsy vibe from central Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nakameguro — one of Tokyo's trendiest neighborhoods built along a canal. Walk the Meguro River canal path lined with cherry blossom trees (late blooms possible in April). Browse independent boutiques, coffee shops, and design studios.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Daikanyama — Nakameguro's chic neighbor. Visit the iconic Tsutaya Books (T-Site) — a beautiful bookstore and lifestyle complex. Explore the Hillside Terrace complex with independent galleries and cafes. Walk to nearby Ebisu for the free Yebisu Beer Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's indie culture hub known for vintage shops, jazz bars, and small theaters. Explore the narrow streets packed with character. Catch a live jazz or indie music performance at one of the small venues.

meals.breakfast: Nakameguro specialty coffee shop — a flat white and pastry for ¥600–800.
meals.lunch: Daikanyama — a trendy but affordable pasta or sandwich cafe for ¥900–1,200.
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — a cozy curry restaurant or yakitori bar for ¥900–1,300.

day_by_day.notes: These three neighborhoods (Nakameguro, Daikanyama, Shimokitazawa) represent Tokyo's cool, creative side. All are within easy subway/walk distance of each other. Shimokitazawa is especially alive on Saturday nights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (book in advance, ¥3,200) — a different and equally stunning immersive digital art experience from teamLab Borderless, focused on water and light. Located on the Yurakucho line near Tsukiji. Arrive at opening (10:00 AM) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toyosu Market (the new Tsukiji) — take a free guided walk through the outer market area and visit the observation deck overlooking the inner wholesale market. Then walk to the Toyosu waterfront for views of the bay and Rainbow Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Tsukiji area — revisit your favorite spots from the trip. Walk through Tsukiji Outer Market one last time and pick up food souvenirs like dried seafood, nori seaweed, and Japanese spices to bring home.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — a final sushi breakfast at your favorite stall for ¥600–900.
meals.lunch: Toyosu area — fresh seafood don (rice bowl) at the market for ¥1,000–1,400.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local Tsukiji izakaya — splurge slightly on a proper seafood set with sake for ¥1,500–2,000.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets is a shorter but equally impressive experience compared to Borderless — book online in advance. Toyosu Market outer area is free to visit. Consider buying food souvenirs tonight to avoid rushing on departure day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — wake up early for one last walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market. Pick up any remaining souvenirs or snacks for the journey home. Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the nearest coin locker (¥400–700) or at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final hours in Tokyo exploring the nearby Ginza area on foot — visit any shops or galleries you missed. Head to Tokyo Station (a short subway ride from Tsukiji) to browse the famous Tokyo Station Character Street for last-minute gifts, and the Gransta underground mall for premium food souvenirs (ekiben, Tokyo Banana, Shiroi Koibito).
day_by_day.evening: Collect luggage and head to the airport via Narita Express or Limousine Bus from Tokyo Station. Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before your flight for transit and check-in.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — tamagoyaki, fresh juice, and a rice ball for ¥400–600.
meals.lunch: Tokyo Station Gransta food court or a quick ramen at a station restaurant for ¥700–900.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or grab a bento box from Tokyo Station to eat on the plane — budget ¥800–1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Coin lockers at Tokyo Station are available in multiple sizes. The Narita Express (N'EX) from Tokyo Station to Narita Airport takes about 55 minutes and costs ¥3,070. Buy an IC card-compatible ticket or use Suica. Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Don't forget to use up remaining Suica balance on food or transfer it before leaving.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use travel time to review itinerary and rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport express (Narita Express or Keikyu Line) to central Tokyo. Check in to your Tsukiji boutique hotel (~15:00–16:00). Freshen up and take a gentle orientation walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tsukiji Outer Market stalls (open until early evening) for a casual introduction to Tokyo street food culture. Browse fresh produce, pickles, tamagoyaki egg stalls, and seafood snacks. Wind down with a relaxed evening stroll along the Sumida River waterfront nearby.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport — try an airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) for an onigiri and green tea (¥300–500)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market street food self-tour: fresh grilled scallops, tamagoyaki skewers, and tuna sashimi bites from market stalls (¥1,500–2,500 total)

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag tip: Stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to help reset your body clock. Keep Day 1 light. IC card (Suica or Pasmo) can be purchased at the airport for easy transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early at the Tsukiji Outer Market for a proper breakfast — this is one of Tokyo's most iconic food experiences. Browse the dozens of vendors selling fresh sushi, grilled seafood, and tamagoyaki. Then walk 10 minutes to the Hamarikyu Gardens, a stunning Edo-period landscape garden with a traditional teahouse on a tidal pond. Enjoy a cup of matcha with a wagashi sweet while overlooking the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Tokyo Water Bus (Sumida River cruise) from Hamarikyu to Asakusa (~40 min, ¥780). Arrive in Asakusa and explore Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Walk through Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. Explore the backstreets of Asakusa for a glimpse of old Shitamachi (downtown) Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Tokyo Skytree (a short walk from Asakusa). Visit the Tembo Deck observation floor at 350m for panoramic city views, especially beautiful at dusk as the city lights come on. Return to Tsukiji area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tuna sushi set or grilled seafood breakfast at Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi (¥2,000–3,500)
meals.lunch: Asakusa — try Asakusa Imahan for beef sukiyaki lunch set or a casual tempura lunch at Daikokuya Tempura (¥1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: Near Tsukiji or Ginza — ramen at a local shop such as Tsukiji Kagura or a tonkatsu set meal (¥1,000–1,800)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens entrance: ¥300. Senso-ji is free. Tokyo Skytree Tembo Deck: ¥2,100 (book online in advance to avoid queues). Water Bus is a scenic and fun alternative to the subway.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Spend the morning exploring multi-story electronics shops like Yodobashi Akiba and BIC Camera, retro game shops, and anime merchandise stores. Visit the Radio Kaikan building for vintage electronics and rare tech collectibles. This is ground zero for Tokyo's otaku and tech culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba island (accessible by Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi, ~30 min). Explore interactive exhibits on robotics, AI, space exploration, and the internet. See the famous ASIMO robot demonstrations and the giant globe display. Spend time on Odaiba's waterfront with views of Rainbow Bridge and a replica Statue of Liberty.
day_by_day.evening: Stay on Odaiba for dinner and explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, which features a life-size Gundam statue outside. Return to Tsukiji via Rinkai Line or Yurikamome.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café — Japanese morning set (toast, egg, salad, coffee) at a local kissaten (coffee shop) for ¥500–800
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a maid café experience for the cultural novelty (¥1,500–2,500 including a drink), or grab a quick curry at CoCo Ichibanya (¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Odaiba — Decks Tokyo Beach food floor for diverse Japanese options including ramen, sushi, and izakaya-style dishes (¥1,500–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan admission: ¥630 adults. Odaiba is best visited in the afternoon/evening when the city lights reflect on the bay. Akihabara is best explored on foot — the main street and side alleys are equally fascinating.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Shinjuku and visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for free panoramic views from the 45th-floor observation deck (opens 09:00). Walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially lovely in April when late cherry blossoms or spring flowers may still be blooming. Enjoy a peaceful morning stroll through French formal, English landscape, and Japanese traditional garden sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Shinjuku neighborhood: visit Takashimaya Times Square department store for Japanese food hall browsing, then walk through the Golden Gai area (best visited in the evening but fascinating to see by day) and Kabukicho entertainment district. Head to the Samurai Museum in Shinjuku for an engaging cultural experience with armor displays and live demonstrations.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku's legendary nightlife district. Start with drinks at a rooftop bar, then explore the narrow alley bars of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — tiny yakitori stalls packed with smoke, grilled skewers, and local atmosphere. A quintessential Tokyo evening.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — pick up onigiri, a hard-boiled egg, and canned coffee from 7-Eleven (¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic-style — grab bento boxes from a nearby convenience store or supermarket and eat in the garden (¥600–1,000)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane), Shinjuku — yakitori skewers, beer, and grilled offal at tiny atmospheric stalls (¥2,000–3,500 with drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free. Shinjuku Gyoen entry: ¥500. Samurai Museum: ¥1,900 (includes English-guided tour). Omoide Yokocho is cash-only at most stalls — bring ¥3,000–5,000 in cash.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku and visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — a serene Shinto shrine set within a forested park. Arrive early to see morning worshippers and experience the peaceful atmosphere under towering cedar trees. Walk the gravel path through the torii gates. Then stroll down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for Tokyo's wildest youth fashion, crepe stands, and pop culture shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Harajuku to Omotesando — Tokyo's most elegant tree-lined boulevard. Browse the flagship stores of Japanese designers (Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons) and international luxury brands. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex (designed by Tadao Ando) for architecture appreciation. Continue to the Nezu Museum for Japanese and Asian antiquities in a beautiful garden setting.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Crossing scramble experience. Visit the Shibuya Sky rooftop observation deck for a spectacular 360-degree view of the crossing and city at night. Explore the vibrant Shibuya Center-gai street.

meals.breakfast: Near Harajuku — Marion Crêpes on Takeshita Street for a sweet crepe (¥500–700) or a café breakfast
meals.lunch: Omotesando area — try a trendy café lunch such as Eggs 'n Things or a Japanese lunch set at a local restaurant (¥1,200–2,000)
meals.dinner: Shibuya — Ichiran Ramen for a solo-booth tonkotsu ramen experience (¥1,000–1,500) or a sushi conveyor belt restaurant (¥1,500–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free. Nezu Museum: ¥1,300. Shibuya Sky observation deck: ¥2,000 (book online — sells out fast). Sunday morning at Meiji Jingu is particularly atmospheric. Harajuku to Omotesando to Shibuya is all walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours from Tokyo via Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa). Arrive in Nikko and head straight to the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — an extraordinarily ornate mausoleum for Tokugawa Ieyasu, Japan's first shogun. Explore the lavishly decorated shrine buildings, the famous 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkeys carving, and the Yomeimon Gate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Nikko shrine and temple complex: visit Futarasan Shrine and Rinno-ji Temple with its giant Buddha statues. Walk to Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River for a classic Nikko photo. If time allows, take a bus up to Kegon Falls — one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo (arrive ~19:00–20:00). Have a relaxed dinner near your hotel in Tsukiji or Ginza.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or a convenience store before departing — onigiri and coffee (¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Nikko — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a Nikko specialty, at a local restaurant near the shrine complex (¥1,200–2,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji or Ginza area — a comforting bowl of udon or soba at a local noodle shop (¥800–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tobu Nikko Line round trip from Asakusa: ~¥2,700. Tosho-gu combined entry: ¥1,300. Start early (depart by 07:30–08:00) to maximize time in Nikko. A Tobu Tourist Pass (¥4,000) covers round-trip train and some buses — worth it for this day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander through Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful in spring with old cherry trees), browse the charming Yanaka Ginza shopping street with its artisan shops and local food stalls. Visit small temples and shrines tucked between traditional wooden houses. This is authentic, unhurried Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the subway to Ueno. Visit the Tokyo National Museum — Japan's largest museum with an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, pottery, and Buddhist sculptures. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the main Honkan building. Walk through Ueno Park (free) and visit Ueno Zoo if interested.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara for an evening of tech culture: visit Super Potato retro gaming store, browse the latest gadgets in Yodobashi Camera, or experience a VR arcade. Try one of the themed cafés in the area.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza — fresh melon bread or a traditional Japanese breakfast snack from a local bakery stall (¥300–600)
meals.lunch: Ueno area — Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko) market street for affordable food stalls: takoyaki, gyoza, or a quick seafood bowl (¥800–1,500)
meals.dinner: Akihabara — try a themed restaurant or a reliable Japanese curry house; Akihabara has many affordable options (¥1,000–2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum admission: ¥1,000. Yanaka is best explored on foot with no fixed plan — getting slightly lost is part of the charm. Yanaka Ginza is quieter on weekday mornings. Bring cash for the Ameyoko market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Visit TeamLab Borderless or TeamLab Planets (book well in advance — these sell out weeks ahead). TeamLab Planets in Toyosu is the more immersive 'walk through art' experience. Spend 2–3 hours in the digital art installations where visitors wade through water and experience rooms of infinite flowers, light, and color. A truly unique intersection of technology and art.
day_by_day.afternoon: After TeamLab, explore the Toyosu Market (the successor to Tsukiji wholesale market). Take the guided observation tour of the tuna auction viewing area (book in advance) or simply visit the market's shops and restaurants for the freshest seafood in Tokyo. Return to the hotel for a rest before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ginza district — Tokyo's most upscale shopping and dining neighborhood, just a short walk or subway ride from Tsukiji. Window shop along Chuo-dori, visit the Itoya stationery flagship store (8 floors of beautiful Japanese stationery and paper goods), and enjoy the elegant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a nearby café — Japanese breakfast set or a bakery near Tsukiji (¥600–1,000)
meals.lunch: Toyosu Market — ultra-fresh sushi or seafood bowl at one of the market's restaurants (¥2,000–3,500 — splurge-worthy)
meals.dinner: Ginza — explore the basement food hall (depachika) of Matsuya or Mitsukoshi department store for gourmet takeaway, or dine at an affordable sushi conveyor belt (¥1,500–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Planets tickets: ¥3,200 (must book online in advance — check availability as soon as possible). Toyosu Market tuna auction viewing is extremely limited and must be booked months ahead through the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website. Ginza Itoya is open until 20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (about 1 hour from Tokyo via JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station). Start at the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in) — the iconic 13.35-meter bronze Amida Buddha statue. You can enter the hollow interior of the statue. Explore the surrounding temple grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through the forested hills to reach Zeniarai Benzaiten Ugafuku Shrine (a cave shrine where washing money is said to multiply it). Continue to Hase-dera Temple with its stunning hilltop garden views over Kamakura Bay and its collection of Jizo statues. Explore Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts and sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Dinner in the Tsukiji or Ginza neighborhood. Take a relaxed evening walk along the Sumida River.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing (¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Kamakura — shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl, a Kamakura specialty, at a restaurant near Hase Station (¥1,200–2,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area — izakaya dinner with small plates: edamame, karaage, grilled fish, and cold beer (¥2,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura round trip from Tokyo: ~¥1,900 (covered by JR Pass if you have one). Great Buddha entry: ¥300. Hase-dera entry: ¥400. Depart by 08:00 to have a full day. Kamakura is hilly — wear comfortable walking shoes. April weather should be pleasant for this trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (a 10-minute subway ride from Tsukiji). This large museum recreates life in Edo-period Tokyo with full-scale reproductions of old bridges, merchant districts, and samurai residences. Excellent for understanding how Tokyo evolved from a feudal city to a modern metropolis. English audio guides available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Ryogoku Kokugikan Sumo Arena nearby. Check if a sumo tournament (basho) is happening in April (the Spring Basho is in March in Osaka, so this may be between tournaments — but you can still visit the Sumo Museum inside the arena, which is free). Walk through the Ryogoku neighborhood, which is full of chanko-nabe (sumo wrestler stew) restaurants. Then head to Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, a hip neighborhood known for its third-wave coffee culture and the Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum garden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ginza or Tsukiji for a special dinner. Visit a depachika (department store basement food hall) for gourmet Japanese food shopping and prepared meals.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a local kissaten café near Tsukiji — Japanese morning set with toast, egg, and coffee (¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Ryogoku — chanko-nabe hot pot at a sumo wrestler restaurant such as Chanko Tomoegata (¥1,500–2,500) — a unique cultural dining experience
meals.dinner: Ginza depachika — assemble a gourmet dinner from department store food halls: premium sashimi, Japanese pickles, wagashi sweets (¥2,000–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Edo-Tokyo Museum admission: ¥600. Sumo Museum is free. Check the Japan Sumo Association website for tournament schedules — if a basho is happening, attending a day of sumo is one of Tokyo's great experiences (tickets from ¥2,200). Kiyosumi-Shirakawa's Blue Bottle Coffee Japan flagship is worth a visit for coffee enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's beloved bohemian neighborhood, known for vintage clothing shops, independent cafés, live music venues, and a creative arts scene. Browse the dozens of second-hand clothing stores, visit record shops, and soak up the laid-back atmosphere that feels completely different from central Tokyo. This is where Tokyo's young creative class lives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nakameguro for an afternoon stroll along the Meguro River canal — lined with cherry trees (possibly still in late bloom in mid-April) and flanked by stylish boutiques, cafés, and galleries. This is one of Tokyo's most photogenic neighborhoods. Visit the Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — a beautifully designed bookstore and lifestyle complex beloved by Tokyo's design community.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special dinner in the Ebisu or Daikanyama area — both are known for excellent mid-range restaurants with a sophisticated atmosphere. Return to Tsukiji via subway.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa — breakfast at a local independent café; try Bear Pond Espresso or a neighborhood café for excellent coffee and toast (¥600–1,000)
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa — casual lunch at a curry restaurant (Japanese curry is a local favorite here) or a ramen shop (¥800–1,500)
meals.dinner: Daikanyama or Ebisu — Japanese-French bistro or a refined izakaya with seasonal Japanese cuisine (¥3,000–5,000 — a slightly elevated dining experience for the penultimate evening)

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is best explored without a fixed plan — wandering is the point. Most vintage shops open around 12:00, so the morning is best for cafés and the neighborhood atmosphere. Nakameguro to Daikanyama is a pleasant 10-minute walk. Daikanyama T-Site is open until 02:00 — a wonderful late-night bookstore experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab or, alternatively, spend the morning at the 21_21 Design Sight museum in Roppongi (designed by Tadao Ando), which hosts cutting-edge Japanese design exhibitions. Then explore the Roppongi Hills complex, including the Mori Art Museum on the 53rd floor — one of Tokyo's best contemporary art museums with a spectacular observation deck (Tokyo City View).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon revisiting your favorite Tokyo neighborhood or any spots you missed. Consider returning to Tsukiji Outer Market for final food shopping — buy Japanese snacks, dried seafood, seaweed, and condiments as gifts or souvenirs. Visit a 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) for affordable, high-quality Japanese goods to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a memorable final meal. Consider a proper sushi omakase experience at a mid-range sushi counter near Tsukiji (the neighborhood is famous for sushi), or a teppanyaki dinner. End the evening with a nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the Tokyo skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — take your time with a proper sit-down breakfast (¥800–1,200)
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills or Mori Building area — café lunch or a Japanese set meal (¥1,200–2,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji/Ginza — mid-range omakase sushi counter (8–10 pieces of chef's selection nigiri) at a local sushi restaurant (¥5,000–8,000 — a special farewell splurge); alternatively, a yakitori dinner for ¥2,500–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View: ¥2,000. 21_21 Design Sight: ¥1,200. For the farewell sushi dinner, restaurants near Tsukiji like Sushi Yoshitake, Sushi Sho, or smaller neighborhood counters offer excellent quality. Book the sushi dinner in advance. Pack souvenirs tonight to make tomorrow morning easier.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Wake up early for one last visit to the Tsukiji Outer Market for breakfast — a fitting full-circle moment from Day 1. Enjoy fresh sushi or a tamagoyaki sandwich one last time. Return to the hotel, complete packing, and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: if early afternoon flight, head directly to the airport after checkout (allow 2–3 hours for travel + check-in + security). If late afternoon/evening flight, store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker at Tokyo Station and spend a few final hours in the Ginza or Marunouchi area — visit the Intermediatheque museum (free with student ID, ¥500 otherwise) in the JP Tower for a unique collection of Tokyo University artifacts, or browse Ginza's galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Tokyo. Take the Narita Express or Keikyu Line to the airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final fresh sushi breakfast or tamagoyaki roll (¥1,500–2,500)
meals.lunch: Airport — treat yourself to a proper Japanese meal at one of Narita or Haneda's excellent terminal restaurants (ramen, sushi, or tonkatsu set, ¥1,200–2,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport travel, check-in, and security. Narita Express from Tokyo Station takes ~60 minutes (¥3,070). Keikyu Line from Shinagawa to Haneda takes ~30 minutes (¥300–600). Coin lockers are available at Tokyo Station and most major stations for storing luggage on your last day (¥300–700 per locker). Don't forget to reclaim any tax-free shopping receipts before leaving Japan.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's culinary soul.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-in: Flight LH lands at Narita/Haneda at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked luxury airport transfer (private car or limousine bus) to your boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tsukiji Outer Market Orientation Stroll: Take a leisurely introductory walk through the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market just steps from your hotel. Sample fresh tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), premium tuna sashimi bites, and artisan street snacks from renowned vendors. Pick up a matcha soft serve from Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime. Get your bearings in the vibrant neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito (or comparable Michelin-starred sushi counter nearby such as Sushi Yoshitake in Ginza): Enjoy an intimate omakase experience featuring the finest seasonal Edomae sushi. Reserve well in advance. Pair with premium sake selected by the chef.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport meal)
meals.lunch: Light bites at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh oysters, grilled scallops, and tamagoyaki from top market stalls
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at a Michelin-starred Ginza sushi counter (e.g., Sushi Yoshitake or Sushi Sho) — budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to jet lag. Confirm hotel concierge has arranged all upcoming reservations. Ginza is a 10-minute taxi ride from Tsukiji — ideal for a first evening out.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (Guided Premium Experience): Join an expert-led small-group or private food tour of Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, uni (sea urchin), wagyu beef skewers, dashi broth, pickles, and seasonal delicacies. Visit hidden vendor stalls and learn the history of Japan's most famous food district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens & Tokyo Bay Cruise: Walk to the stunning Hamarikyu Gardens (5 minutes from Tsukiji), a traditional feudal garden with tidal ponds and cherry blossom trees. Board a scenic Sumida River water bus from Hamarikyu Pier to Asakusa, enjoying panoramic views of the Tokyo skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa: Visit Senso-ji Temple illuminated at dusk, stroll Nakamise shopping street for premium artisan souvenirs. Dinner at Kawachiya, a historic kappo restaurant in Asakusa serving refined traditional Japanese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Tsukiji market breakfast — fresh fish rice bowls (kaisendon) at Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime
meals.lunch: Market tastings during the food tour serve as a substantial late-morning meal; supplement with a matcha latte and wagashi (Japanese sweets)
meals.dinner: Kappo or kaiseki dinner in Asakusa — refined multi-course Japanese cuisine, budget ¥15,000–¥25,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the private Tsukiji food tour in advance through a premium operator (e.g., Arigato Japan Food Tours or a bespoke concierge service). Hamarikyu Gardens admission is ¥300.

day_by_day.morning: Ginza Art & Culture Morning: Explore the upscale Ginza district on foot. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (a Tokyo institution), browse the Ginza Six luxury mall's rooftop garden, and stop into the Shiseido Gallery for contemporary art. Admire the architecture of flagship boutiques by global luxury brands.
day_by_day.afternoon: teamLab Planets (Toyosu) or teamLab Borderless (if re-opened at new Azabudai Hills location): Immerse yourself in world-renowned digital art installations by the avant-garde collective teamLab — a perfect intersection of technology, culture, and art. Book timed-entry tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Toyosu Fish Market Observation Deck (optional late-afternoon add-on), then head to Roppongi for dinner. Dine at Azabu Juban's acclaimed restaurant or Roppongi's Joel Robuchon Tokyo (French-Japanese fusion in a stunning château setting).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café de l'Ambre in Ginza — a legendary Tokyo coffee institution
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ginza Kojyu or Ginza Kyubey (premium sushi lunch set) — budget ¥8,000–¥15,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo or The Restaurant by Joël Robuchon, Roppongi — budget ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online immediately. Ginza to Toyosu is a short taxi or subway ride. Roppongi is accessible by taxi from Toyosu in 20 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Tech & Pop Culture Deep Dive: Take the subway to Akihabara, Tokyo's legendary electronics and otaku culture district. Visit Yodobashi Camera (multi-floor electronics megastore), explore cutting-edge gadget shops, retro game arcades, and the latest in Japanese tech innovation. Visit the AKB48 Theater area and iconic maid cafés for cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sony Park & Sony Showroom (Ginza) or Panasonic Center Tokyo: Experience Japan's tech culture at its finest. Sony Park in Ginza features interactive brand experiences and pop-up exhibitions. Alternatively, visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba island — home to ASIMO robots and cutting-edge science exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Odaiba Waterfront Evening: If visiting Miraikan, stay in Odaiba for the evening. Enjoy the futuristic waterfront cityscape, visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, and dine with views of the Rainbow Bridge. Return to Tsukiji by water taxi or Yurikamome monorail.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium Japanese breakfast set at a nearby café in Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch at a high-end ramen shop (e.g., Fuunji-style tsukemen) or a themed restaurant — budget ¥2,000–¥4,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tableaux in Daikanyama or a premium teppanyaki restaurant in Odaiba with Rainbow Bridge views — budget ¥15,000–¥25,000

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best visited on weekdays or early Saturday morning before crowds peak. Miraikan requires advance booking for robot demonstrations. Odaiba is accessible via the Yurikamome line from Shimbashi.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka Historic District Morning Walk: Discover one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods. Stroll through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, visit Yanaka Cemetery (famous for cherry blossoms in spring), explore traditional temples, artisan craft shops, and independent galleries. A rare glimpse of pre-war Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ueno Cultural Afternoon: Walk to Ueno Park and visit the Tokyo National Museum — Japan's largest museum, home to an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, ancient ceramics, and Buddhist sculpture. Stroll through Ueno Park's cherry blossom paths (late blooms possible in mid-April).
day_by_day.evening: Kagurazaka French-Japanese Quarter: Head to Kagurazaka, Tokyo's charming Franco-Japanese neighborhood. Explore cobblestone alleyways (yokocho), traditional geisha establishments, and French bistros. Dine at a premium French-Japanese fusion restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a traditional kissaten (old-school Tokyo coffee shop) in Yanaka — toast, eggs, and coffee set
meals.lunch: Lunch at Izu-ei in Ueno — a legendary unaju (eel over rice) restaurant established in 1807, budget ¥5,000–¥8,000
meals.dinner: Dinner in Kagurazaka at Kagurazaka Ishikawa (Michelin 3-star kaiseki) — budget ¥35,000–¥55,000 per person; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays — Sunday is ideal. Kagurazaka Ishikawa is one of Tokyo's most celebrated kaiseki restaurants; reservations are essential months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya & Harajuku Cultural Exploration: Take the subway to Shibuya. Visit the famous Shibuya Crossing (best viewed from Starbucks Reserve Roastery Tokyo or Mag's Park). Explore the newly developed Shibuya Sky observation deck for panoramic city views. Walk to Harajuku's Takeshita Street for youth culture and fashion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Omotesando Architecture & Design Walk: Stroll along Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's Champs-Élysées. Admire landmark buildings by Tadao Ando (Omotesando Hills), Toyo Ito, and other world-class architects. Visit the Nezu Museum and its exquisite bamboo garden for a peaceful cultural interlude.
day_by_day.evening: Daikanyama & Nakameguro Evening: Walk or taxi to Daikanyama's T-Site (a stunning bookstore and cultural complex by Klein Dytham Architecture). Stroll the Nakameguro canal lined with boutiques and cafés. Dine at a premium restaurant along the canal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Shibuya's Starbucks Reserve Roastery Tokyo — a multi-floor coffee experience with premium single-origin brews
meals.lunch: Lunch at Omotesando's Maison Landemaine (French bakery) or a premium ramen experience at Afuri Omotesando — budget ¥2,000–¥5,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nakameguro's Sushi Saito annex or Inua (if available) — Nordic-Japanese cuisine, budget ¥20,000–¥35,000

day_by_day.notes: Nezu Museum is closed on Mondays — substitute with the Ota Memorial Museum of Art (ukiyo-e prints) in Harajuku which is open. Daikanyama T-Site is a must-visit for design and book lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nikko (Optional) or Shinjuku Morning: Option A — Take the Tobu Nikko Limited Express from Asakusa for a full-day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Nikko: visit the ornate Tosho-gu Shrine, Rinno-ji Temple, and Kegon Falls. Option B — Explore Shinjuku's Kabukicho district by day, visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free), and browse Isetan department store.
day_by_day.afternoon: If Nikko: Explore the cedar-lined avenues, Futarasan Shrine, and Taiyuin Mausoleum. If Shinjuku: Visit the Samurai Museum for an immersive cultural experience, then explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (stunning in spring).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo (if Nikko day trip) and dine in Shinjuku. Visit the atmospheric Golden Gai alleyways for pre-dinner drinks at a tiny, intimate bar. Dine at Kozue (Park Hyatt Tokyo, 40th floor) for refined Japanese cuisine with Mt. Fuji views.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or onigiri from a premium convenience store for the Nikko train journey
meals.lunch: If Nikko: Lunch at Meiji-no-Yakata restaurant near Tosho-gu (Western-Japanese fusion in a historic building). If Shinjuku: Lunch at a premium soba restaurant (Sunaba Soba) — budget ¥3,000–¥6,000
meals.dinner: Kozue at Park Hyatt Tokyo, Shinjuku — Japanese cuisine with panoramic city views, budget ¥20,000–¥30,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Nikko round trip takes approximately 4–5 hours of travel; depart by 7:30am. The Lost in Translation Bar (New York Bar) at Park Hyatt is iconic for an after-dinner nightcap — cover charge applies.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji to Nihonbashi Cultural Morning: Explore the historic Nihonbashi district, Tokyo's original commercial heart. Visit Mitsukoshi department store (Japan's oldest, founded 1673), the Bank of Japan Currency Museum, and the elegant Nihonbashi bridge. Browse Coredo Muromachi for premium Japanese crafts and foods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tokyo Station & Marunouchi District: Visit the beautifully restored Tokyo Station (1914 red-brick building). Explore the underground Gransta shopping complex for premium regional foods and gifts. Walk through the Marunouchi business district to the Imperial Palace East Gardens — serene traditional gardens open to the public.
day_by_day.evening: Kyobashi & Ginza Art Gallery Hop: Visit Artizon Museum (Bridgestone Collection) in Kyobashi for world-class Western and Japanese modern art. Then stroll through Ginza's gallery district for contemporary art. Dine at Ginza Kojyu or Sushi Saito for a refined evening meal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Nihonbashi Yukari — a renowned traditional Japanese restaurant offering premium morning sets
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nihonbashi Tamai — a historic eel (unagi) restaurant established in 1910, budget ¥6,000–¥10,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ginza Kojyu (Michelin 3-star kaiseki) — budget ¥35,000–¥55,000; or Sushi Saito if reservation available

day_by_day.notes: Imperial Palace East Gardens are free to enter and closed on Mondays and Fridays. Artizon Museum has a premium collection and is rarely crowded — a hidden gem.

day_by_day.morning: Odaiba & Future Technology Morning: Head to Odaiba via Yurikamome monorail. Visit the Toyota Mega Web showroom (interactive automotive technology experience) and the Panasonic Center Tokyo for smart home and energy technology exhibits. Experience the futuristic urban planning of this man-made island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miraikan — National Museum of Emerging Science: Spend the afternoon at Miraikan exploring exhibitions on AI, space exploration, robotics (ASIMO demonstrations), genomics, and the future of human civilization. One of the world's finest science museums.
day_by_day.evening: Odaiba Waterfront Sunset & Dinner: Watch the sunset behind the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline from Odaiba Beach. Dine at a premium restaurant in the Venus Fort or DiverCity complex, or take a water bus back to Hinode Pier and dine in Shiodome or Ginza.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium egg sandwich from Tsukiji's Tamago Yaki specialists
meals.lunch: Lunch at Odaiba's Bills (Australian brunch institution with Tokyo Bay views) or a premium ramen bar — budget ¥3,000–¥6,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tableaux Daikanyama or a premium steakhouse in Ginza (e.g., Kawamura Ginza for A5 wagyu) — budget ¥25,000–¥40,000

day_by_day.notes: Book Miraikan robot demonstration slots online in advance. Toyota Mega Web is free to enter. The water bus from Odaiba to Hinode Pier offers beautiful bay views at sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Shrine & Yoyogi Park: Start the day at the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku — walk the forested gravel path, participate in a traditional purification ritual, and observe the architecture of this Shinto masterpiece. Stroll through Yoyogi Park, popular with locals on weekends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shibuya Scramble Square & Tech Retail: Visit Shibuya Scramble Square's SHIBUYA SKY observation deck for 360° views. Explore Shibuya's Loft and Tokyu Hands stores for premium Japanese lifestyle products, stationery, and gadgets. Visit Bic Camera for cutting-edge electronics.
day_by_day.evening: Ebisu & Daikanyama Premium Dining: Head to the upscale Ebisu neighborhood. Visit Yebisu Beer Museum (free, with premium tasting options). Dine at one of Ebisu's acclaimed restaurants for a relaxed, sophisticated evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a premium hotel café in Harajuku or Omotesando (e.g., Café Kitsuné Aoyama)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shibuya's Ukai-tei (premium teppanyaki with A5 wagyu) — budget ¥15,000–¥25,000
meals.dinner: Dinner at Château Restaurant Joël Robuchon in Ebisu (formal French fine dining in a stunning château) — budget ¥30,000–¥50,000

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is best visited early morning before crowds arrive. SHIBUYA SKY tickets should be booked online. Château Restaurant Joël Robuchon requires formal attire and advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Kyoto Day Trip — Fushimi Inari & Gion: Take the Nozomi Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo Station to Kyoto (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes). Visit the iconic Fushimi Inari Taisha shrine with its thousands of vermillion torii gates — hike the forest trail for stunning views and fewer crowds at the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gion & Higashiyama District: Stroll through Gion, Kyoto's famous geisha district. Walk the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes lined with traditional machiya townhouses. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple perched on the hillside with panoramic views of Kyoto.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo: Board the Shinkansen back to Tokyo (last Nozomi trains depart around 21:00). Enjoy a premium ekiben (train bento) purchased at Kyoto Station for the return journey. Arrive back in Tokyo and relax at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or onigiri for the Shinkansen journey
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kyoto at Kikunoi Roan (Michelin-starred kaiseki lunch) near Higashiyama — budget ¥8,000–¥15,000
meals.dinner: Premium ekiben on the Shinkansen (Kyoto-style obento) or a late-night ramen at a Tokyo station restaurant upon return

day_by_day.notes: Purchase reserved Shinkansen seats in advance via the JR Pass or at the station. Depart Tokyo by 7:00–8:00am to maximize time in Kyoto. This is an optional day trip — alternatively, explore more of Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Sumida River Morning & Asakusa Revisited: Take a peaceful morning walk along the Sumida River. Cross the Azuma Bridge to Asakusa and visit Senso-ji Temple in the morning light. Explore the premium craft shops of Nakamise-dori for final souvenir shopping — lacquerware, hand-forged knives, washi paper, and ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tokyo Skytree: Visit Tokyo Skytree, the world's tallest broadcasting tower (634m). Purchase tickets for the Tembo Deck (350m) and Tembo Galleria (450m) for breathtaking panoramic views of Tokyo and, on clear days, Mount Fuji. Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Omakase Dinner: Celebrate the penultimate evening with a grand farewell omakase dinner at one of Tokyo's finest sushi or kaiseki restaurants. Consider Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza, if reservation possible), Saito, or Ryugin for a memorable finale.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Asakusa's Daikokuya Tempura — a legendary tempura restaurant open since 1887, serving premium breakfast sets
meals.lunch: Lunch at Solamachi (Tokyo Skytree base) — explore the premium food hall for regional Japanese specialties, budget ¥3,000–¥6,000
meals.dinner: Grand farewell omakase at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten or Ryugin (modern Japanese kaiseki) — budget ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Skytree tickets can be purchased in advance online to avoid queues. Ryugin by Chef Seiji Yamamoto is a world-renowned kaiseki destination — book months in advance. Ginza's Sukiyabashi Jiro requires connections or concierge assistance to reserve.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Tsukiji: Enjoy a leisurely final morning in your home neighborhood. Return to Tsukiji Outer Market one last time for a farewell breakfast of fresh sushi, grilled seafood, and tamagoyaki. Browse specialty shops for premium Japanese pantry items to take home — dashi, wasabi, premium soy sauce, and matcha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-Minute Shopping & Departure Prep: Head to Ginza for any final luxury shopping (Mikimoto pearls, premium Japanese whisky at The Whisky Shop, high-end Japanese stationery). Return to hotel to collect luggage. Arrange private airport transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Allow 3+ hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure: Board your return flight, reflecting on 13 extraordinary days of Tokyo's finest food, technology, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — premium kaisendon (seafood rice bowl) with uni, ikura, and toro at Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime
meals.lunch: Premium airport dining at Narita or Haneda — both airports have excellent Japanese restaurant options including sushi, ramen, and tonkatsu
meals.dinner: In-flight (business/first class)

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — Narita is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Pack any food souvenirs carefully per customs regulations (no fresh fish or meat allowed into most countries). Keep receipts for tax-free purchases for customs refund at the airport.
